H10.description: _effort_on_wire hardcodes 'CLI passes through, anthropic maps, everyone else None' instead of asking the dispatching adapter, so MODELINV effort_effective is wrong for providers whose type differs from the key or for CLI adapters that do not send effort.

H11.description: A single-hop chain refused by the agy opt-in gets verdict-quality reason 'Other' instead of a distinct opt-in reason.

H16.description: The calibration hint always names the failing hop's model id unquoted, so a CLI hop gets a probe command the probe refuses and the model id is not shell-quoted.

H21.description: effort_effective is computed inline in the _emit_modelinv call, so an exception there falls into the emit handler and the whole MODELINV envelope is lost.

H22.description: The final emit derives effort_effective inline (an exception loses the envelope) and omits models_not_planned.

H200.description: A tokens-per-minute 429 is retried on the 5 s/15 s schedule, which cannot clear the 60 s window, so a transient throttle persists and is mis-recorded.

H201.description: _STATUS_5XX matches any bare 5xx number (e.g. 'took 503 ms'), classifying non-transient failures as transient.

H202.description: Operator- and CLI-supplied values (host route, resolved cli_model, cli --version) reach the catalog's YAML text and provenance comment unchecked, so a line break or control character can corrupt or inject catalog content.

H203.description: subprocess.run(timeout=) kills only the direct child (the wrapper), leaving the real claude process running, and output past 1 MB is silently truncated into a classification.

H204.description: An exception inside _classify propagates as a traceback and loses the probe record after paid attempts.

H206.description: The classifier truncates the diagnostic to 300 chars before classifying and checks the context-limit marker first, so Bedrock's 'Too many tokens, please wait' throttle is recorded as a size rejection with no retry.

H207.description: Transient markers are searched in the truncated diagnostic only.

H208.description: Writer signature gains required probe_outcome / sample_size.

H209.description: write_catalog_operator_set has no probe_outcome and validates none of its provenance fields, so any caller can write a partial or unvalidated probe as if it were clean.

H210.description: The writer hardcodes sample_size: null and omits probe_outcome in ceiling_calibration.

H212.description: The line-level catalog edit is returned without re-parsing, so a malformed write or a change outside the entry would be persisted.

H214.description: --allow-partial, --tier and --itpm are silently ignored with --transport claude-headless, so the operator believes they took effect.

H215.description: A bound bracketed by a token-budget/throttle rejection (not a context limit) is judged clean and can be written as the context ceiling.

H216.description: A token-limit 429 that persists over the short retries is turned into a size rejection even though the TPM window was never waited out, and retry-after hints are ignored (the hunk also adds the per-attempt charge table).

H217.description: Validates the new partial-write flag's dependency.

H218.description: The budget estimate uses the plain input price (the CLI bills the cache-write rate, 1.25x) and a 1.0 tokenizer ratio, and catalog write prerequisites/provenance are only checked after money has been spent.

H219.description: The per-attempt budget pre-check estimates the first blind step at ratio 1.0, under-estimating the cost of the 4.7+ tokenizer.

H220.description: The retry sleep always uses the short backoff regardless of class or retry-after hint.

H221.description: Spend charges every failed attempt (including CLI-local rejections never sent, spawn failures) at the full estimate and does not handle an output-cap overflow or an interrupt mid-attempt, so spend and budget stops are wrong.

H222.description: The bisection loop is unguarded: ^C or an unexpected exception after paid steps exits without writing the record.

H223.description: The outcome reasons never record an interrupted bisection.

H224.description: The tracked probe record stores the raw cli_bin and argv (absolute home paths) and re-resolves cli_model, not the binary that actually ran.

H225.description: The record claims written_ceiling before the catalog write is attempted, so a failed atomic write leaves a record saying the bound was written.

H226.description: There is no exit path for an interrupted bisection, so it falls through the partial/clean handling with the wrong exit code.

H227.description: Removes the late catalog write now done before the record is serialized.
